annotation.summary_en: Russian criminal-law article on who bears criminal responsibility when an autonomous surgical robot harms a patient. It rejects robots and "electronic personhood" as criminal subjects, points to developers/programmers (negligence) and manufacturers, and warns that the lack of legal regulation risks misattributing liability.
key_provisions_or_claims: Robots cannot be criminal subjects: the subject must be a sane natural person of age, and robot guilt cannot be proven.
Four manufacturer/cyber-physical system reasonableness scenarios; the fourth (reasonable manufacturer, unreasonable system) is unresolved.
Developers or programmers may be liable for negligence when the fault is in the system.
Autonomous surgery (e.g., STAR) makes responsibility gaps more pressing.
Absence of regulation risks punishing the wrong persons and letting responsible ones escape.
annotation.title_clean: Роботы в хирургии: кто должен нести уголовную ответственность
annotation.title_en: Robots in surgery: who should be held criminally responsible
